item.title: EXPLAINED: How to take long-term leave from work in Sweden
item.description: Most people have probably felt at some point that they'd benefit from a long-term break from their work, and in Sweden there are several ways you can do that, safe in the knowledge that your job will be waiting for you when you return.

item.title: What's happening with the American takeover of Sweden's Northvolt?
item.description: In March 2025 Swedish electric battery manufacturer Northvolt became the largest bankruptcy case in modern Swedish history. An American company has now bought Northvolt's assets and is starting to rehire in Sweden – but is the sale even finalized?

item.title: Where in Sweden are schools and transport affected by the snow?
item.description: The worst of this week's heavy snowfall appears to be over in the Gothenburg region, but cities along Sweden's northeast coast remain affected. Here's a list of the municipalities where schools remain closed and traffic affected.

item.title: REPORT: Immigrants now even more willing to risk lives to defend Sweden
item.description: People with foreign backgrounds in troubled suburbs are more willing than people with a Swedish background living elsewhere in the country to put their lives at risk and defend Sweden in the event of a military attack, according to a new survey.

item.title: How to get compensation if you're hit by a power cut in Sweden
item.description: Many of the thousands of households in Sweden which have been affected by storm-related power cuts in recent weeks could be eligible for compensation, ranging from a few thousand to tens of thousands of kronor. How does it work?

item.title: 'Let's not kick people out of Sweden who are already contributing'
item.description: Niels Paarup-Petersen, the Centre Party’s newly appointed migration spokesperson, has told The Local why he expects opposition to the government’s tightening of migration laws to grow in the coming year as more and more immigrants people know personally start to be affected.

item.title: Sweden's government to submit new work permit law to parliament 'in a couple of weeks'
item.description: Sweden's government is planning to submit a new bill to parliament that will see the minimum salary for a work permit rise to 90 percent of the median wage, Migration Minister Johan Forssell has told The Local.

item.title: EU countries override France to greenlight Mercosur trade deal
item.description: The EU gave the long-delayed go ahead on Friday to a huge trade deal with South American bloc Mercosur championed by business groups but loathed by many European farmers -- overriding opposition led by France.

item.title: Sweden proposes new plan for stopping mismanaged free schools
item.description: Free school leaders who have mismanaged their schools will be temporarily banned from expanding or starting new schools, a new inquiry has proposed.

item.title: 'I thought if I worked really, really hard, I'd have a chance of staying in Sweden'
item.description: Fereshteh Javani, a campaigner against the abolition of Sweden's track-change law, has told The Local of the year of extra long hours she went through in a battle to meet the work permit salary threshold, only to then have her right to a work permit stripped away from her anyway.
